title: Bifibrant simplicial nerves present coherent model localizations
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use spaces and infinity-category conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. A model category here is complete and cocomplete, with retract-closed classes $C,F,W$, two-out-of-three for $W$, and functorial weak factorization systems $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$. A weak factorization system means factorization of every arrow and mutually characterized left and right diagonal-lifting classes. Cofibrant and fibrant mean that the initial and terminal maps lie in $C$ and $F$, respectively. A simplicial model category is enriched, tensored and cotensored over Kan-model simplicial sets, with the induced mapping-space map for a cofibration and a fibration a Kan fibration, trivial if either input arrow is also a weak equivalence.

Let $\mathcal M$ be such a simplicial model category and let $\mathcal M^{cf}$ be its full simplicial subcategory of cofibrant fibrant objects. For a simplicial category $\mathcal C$, $N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal C$ denotes its homotopy coherent nerve: its $n$-simplices are simplicial functors from the simplicial thickening of $[n]$ to $\mathcal C$. The thickening has objects $0,\ldots,n$ and mapping simplicial sets the ordinary nerves of the posets of subsets of $[i,j]$ containing both endpoints; composition is union, and the mapping set is empty for $i>j$. Then $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{cf})$ is an infinity category and there is an equivalence
$$N(\mathcal M)[W^{-1}]_\infty\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{cf})$$
whose inverse agrees on bifibrant objects with their inclusion into $\mathcal M$ followed by localization. The left side is universal at the level of entire functor infinity categories: for every infinity category $\mathcal E$, restriction identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathcal M)[W^{-1}]_\infty,\mathcal E)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathcal M),\mathcal E)$ on functors inverting $W$. Inclusions of the ordinary full subcategories of cofibrant, fibrant or bifibrant objects induce equivalences of their infinity localizations with this localization. For cofibrant $X$ and fibrant $Y$, the enriched simplicial mapping set $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)$ represents $\operatorname{Map}(qX,qY)$ naturally in the localized variables, and this comparison respects compositions wherever the enriched compositions are defined. In particular, for functorial replacements $QX\to X$ and $Y\to RY$, derived mapping spaces are represented by $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(QX,RY)$. The nerve of the simplicial category of small Kan complexes with their simplicial mapping sets is the resulting model of the infinity category $\mathcal S$ of small spaces.

maintenance_retracted_split.reason: Circular foundation decomposition: this proof uses coherent-nerve comparison and hammock localization, whose straightening/descent and model-colimit comparison proofs require simplicial product inversion, which requires the derived exponential. The exponential's bifibrant mapping-space test uses this statement, closing the delivery cycle. Withdraw this decomposition and stage-1 completion; retain the statement as an unresolved lemma.

proof.text: Work in larger fixed universes as permitted in the statement. Functorial factorization gives a trivial fibration $QX\to X$ with $QX$ cofibrant and a trivial cofibration $X\to RX$ with $RX$ fibrant. Naturality and two-out-of-three imply that $Q$ and $R$ preserve weak equivalences. Apply [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] to the ordinary categories in question. Its hypothesis holds: an isomorphism has the left lifting property against every map, so it lies in the lifting-characterized class $C\cap W\subseteq W$; in particular every identity is in $W$, and two-out-of-three makes $W$ closed under composition. The same holds for $W$ restricted to the full subcategories of cofibrant, fibrant or bifibrant objects, so each is a wide subcategory containing every identity. Inclusion of cofibrant objects has relative inverse $Q$, using the weak natural map $Q\to\mathrm{id}$; inclusion of fibrant objects has relative inverse $R$, using $\mathrm{id}\to R$. For bifibrant objects use $T=RQ$ and the weak natural zigzag $\mathrm{id}\leftarrow Q\to RQ$ in $\mathcal M$. On bifibrant inputs $QX$ is also fibrant, since $QX\to X\to *$ is a composite of fibrations; $RQX$ is also cofibrant, since $0\to QX\to RQX$ is a composite of cofibrations. Thus the restricted zigzag lies inside the bifibrant subcategory. Weak natural transformations become equivalences of functors by the full functor-category universal property and the componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Each inclusion therefore induces an equivalence of infinity localizations. This proves the three inclusion clauses using actual relative inverse functors, without assuming that the ordinary localization models the infinity localization.

source.place: Remark 1.3.4.16, printed p. 116; functorial replacement zigzags and full localization universal property.

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal C$ be the full simplicial category of cofibrant objects. It has interval tensors $I X=X\otimes\Delta^1$. Indeed, SM7 for $0\to X$ says that $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,-)$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations; by the tensor adjunction and diagonal lifting, $X\otimes-$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $\varnothing\to\Delta^1$ is a cofibration and either endpoint $\Delta^0\to\Delta^1$ is a trivial cofibration: it is a monomorphism, and its realization is an inclusion of a point into a contractible interval. Consequently $I X$ is cofibrant and $X\to I X$ is a trivial cofibration. Its retraction $p_X:I X\to X$ belongs to $W$ by two-out-of-three. The class $W$ of weak equivalences between cofibrant objects contains all isomorphisms, by the lifting argument of Step 1, and satisfies two-out-of-three, since all three objects involved are cofibrant. The enriched tensor adjunction supplies exactly the simplicial isomorphism and constant-identity projection required in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-localization]. Thus that lemma gives the coherent comparison
$$N(\mathcal M^c)[W^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathcal D[V^{-1}]_\infty,\qquad \mathcal D=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R_{\mathrm{loc}}\mathcal C),$$
where $V$ consists of the images of the weak equivalences between cofibrant objects. Here $R_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the mappingwise locally Kan replacement, distinct from model-category fibrant replacement $R$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.4.7 hypotheses (3)-(4), applied in the proof of Theorem 1.3.4.20, printed p. 120.

proof.text:
SM7 with $0\to X$ and $Y\to *$ makes $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Y)$ Kan whenever $X$ is cofibrant and $Y$ fibrant. Therefore $\mathcal B=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{cf})$ is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The enriched inclusion followed by locally Kan replacement gives a coherent functor $j:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$. The same node identifies its mapping maps with the weak equivalences
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)\longrightarrow(R_{\mathrm{loc}}\mathcal C)(X,Y)\quad(X,Y\in\mathcal M^{cf}).$$
Thus $j$ is fully faithful. For any cofibrant $X$, choose a trivial cofibration $u_X:X\to RX$ with $RX$ fibrant, hence bifibrant. For every bifibrant $Z$, SM7 says that precomposition
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(RX,Z)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Z)$$
is a trivial Kan fibration. Natural mapping-space comparison for the coherent nerve consequently identifies $j(-)\circ u_X:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(RX,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(X,jZ)$ as an equivalence. All hypotheses of [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] now hold for $j$, giving a coherent adjoint $L\dashv j$ with unit and counit. In particular this constructs the coherent functor; objectwise replacement alone was not taken to be an enriched functor. Its unit at $X$ can be identified with $u_X$ followed by $j$ of an equivalence $RX\simeq LX$: both are universal arrows, so the mapping-space equivalences give mutually inverse maps between their representing objects, compatible with the arrows from $X$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 1.3.4.20, printed p. 120, construction of the left adjoint to the bifibrant inclusion; Kerodon 02FV (not a Stacks tag).

proof.text: We check that $L$ inverts $V$. For $w:X\to Y$ a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects, use [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to write $w=pi$ with $i:X\to T$ a cofibration, $p:T\to Y$ a trivial fibration, and a cofibration section $s:Y\to T$ satisfying $ps=1_Y$. Two-out-of-three makes both $i$ and $s$ trivial cofibrations. For every bifibrant $Z$, SM7 makes $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(i,Z)$ and $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(s,Z)$ trivial Kan fibrations. Since $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(s,Z)\,\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(p,Z)=1$, two-out-of-three in simplicial sets [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(p,Z)$ a weak equivalence as well. Thus precomposition with $w$ is a weak equivalence of Kan complexes. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] and the natural adjunction equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion], precomposition with $Lw$ is an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(LY,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(LX,Z)$ for every $Z$. This implies that $Lw$ is invertible: on components use $Z=LX$ to obtain $g$ with $gLw=1$; injectivity for $Z=LY$ applied to $(Lw)g$ and $1$ gives $(Lw)g=1$. These equations in the homotopy category give an equivalence by the definition of an equivalence. Hence $L(V)$ consists of equivalences.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 1.3.4.20, printed p. 120: the reflector carries weak equivalences to equivalences; Brown split argument expands this check.

proof.text: We prove the required full universal property of $L$. Since $j$ is fully faithful, the adjunction counit $\epsilon:Lj\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$ is an equivalence: its induced maps on mapping spaces are the adjunction equivalences followed by the fully faithful comparison. For a component $\epsilon_b:Ljb\to b$, precomposition therefore gives bijections $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,z)\to\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(Ljb,z)$ for every $z$. With $z=Ljb$, choose $g:b\to Ljb$ such that $g\epsilon_b\simeq1_{Ljb}$. With $z=b$, injectivity and $(\epsilon_b g)\epsilon_b\simeq\epsilon_b=1_b\epsilon_b$ imply $\epsilon_b g\simeq1_b$. Thus $\epsilon_b$ is an equivalence by the stated definition. Let $\mathcal E$ be any infinity category. Precomposition with $L$ maps $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal B,\mathcal E)$ into $\operatorname{Fun}_V(\mathcal D,\mathcal E)$ by Step 4; precomposition with $j$ is a functor in the opposite direction. Their first composite is equivalent to the identity by $\epsilon$. For $G$ inverting $V$, the transformation $G\eta:G\to GjL$ is componentwise an equivalence: by Step 3 each $\eta_X$ is the composite of the image of $u_X\in W$ and an equivalence, and $G$ inverts both. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] turns this into an equivalence in the full functor category. Whiskering the coherent unit and counit supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] makes these comparisons natural also in transformations between functors. Therefore $L$ is universal for inverting $V$ on entire functor infinity categories, and $\mathcal D[V^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathcal B$. A comparison of cores alone is not used.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 1.3.4.20, printed p. 120; expanded reflective-localization argument on full functor categories.

proof.text:
Combine Steps 1, 2 and 5. The composite
$$N(\mathcal M^c)\longrightarrow\mathcal D\xrightarrow{L}\mathcal B$$
is the infinity localization at $W$, and the cofibrant inclusion identifies it with $N(\mathcal M)[W^{-1}]_\infty$. On the ordinary bifibrant subcategory the first functor is $j$ composed with its ordinary-to-coherent nerve map; the counit $Lj\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$ from Step 5 identifies the composite there with that map. The equivalence on localizations of the bifibrant inclusion from Step 1 consequently says exactly that the inverse equivalence $\mathcal B\to N(\mathcal M)[W^{-1}]_\infty$ restricts to the stated inclusion followed by localization. Both agreement and extension are coherent by the full functor-category universal property in [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. The universal property required in the statement is the resulting equivalence of full functor infinity categories.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20 and Remark 1.3.4.16, printed pp. 116-117 and proof p. 120.

proof.text:
For a cofibrant $X$ and fibrant $Y$, choose the trivial fibration $QY\to Y$. Its source is bifibrant, since a fibration to a fibrant object has fibrant source. SM7 makes
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,QY)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Y)$$
a trivial Kan fibration. The mapping-space weak equivalence into the locally Kan replacement, together with [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], identifies the left side with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(X,jQY)$; by the natural adjunction mapping equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion], this is $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(LX,QY)$. Steps 1 and 6 identify it with $\operatorname{Map}(qX,qY)$. These comparisons are natural: the enriched mapping bifunctor, functorial $Q$, natural coherent-nerve comparison, adjunction and localization equivalence all supply their maps before inversion of these weak equivalences. Thus they extend to the localized variables; no choice of unrelated equivalences of spaces is made.

For composition, first consider a cofibrant $X$, bifibrant $Y$ and fibrant $Z$, the restrictions making both factors of the asserted mapping comparison apply. Choose a bifibrant $QZ\to Z$ and a trivial cofibration $X\to RX$ to a bifibrant object. The enriched composition diagrams with sources $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(RX,Y)\times\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(Y,QZ)$ and targets $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(RX,QZ)$ commute strictly with precomposition $X\to RX$ and postcomposition $QZ\to Z$. SM7 makes each needed pre- and postcomposition comparison map a trivial Kan fibration. On the three bifibrant objects the coherent-nerve comparison explicitly preserves composition and its homotopies. The commuting diagrams and equivalences therefore give the requested composition compatibility for $X,Y,Z$ as well, and the natural comparisons carry its higher homotopies. For arbitrary objects replace the first variable by $QX$ and the second by $RY$; the weak replacement maps become equivalences after localization, giving the displayed derived-mapping formula.

proof.text: Apply the result to simplicial sets with the functorial Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and Cartesian tensor, cotensor and function complex. To verify the simplicial axiom, transpose a lifting problem for the induced function-complex map against a horn or boundary inclusion. It is exactly the lifting problem for a fibration against the Cartesian pushout product of the given cofibration with that horn or boundary. A pushout product of monomorphisms is a monomorphism, since its source is the union of two simplicial subsets of the product. Against a horn inclusion $j$, this $j$ is a trivial cofibration by the horn-generation description in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], hence anodyne by the weak factorization system. Since the given cofibration $i$ is monic, [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] makes $i\mathbin{\square}j$ anodyne. If $i$ is trivial and $j$ is a boundary inclusion, the same cited statement applies to $j\mathbin{\square}i$; swapping product factors induces an isomorphism of this arrow with $i\mathbin{\square}j$, so it too has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration. These horn and boundary lifting tests prove that the function-complex map is a fibration, and a trivial fibration when $i$ is trivial. When the given fibration is trivial, its right lifting property against every monomorphism instead applies to $i\mathbin{\square}j$ for every boundary inclusion $j$, including $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing\to\Delta^0$. This proves the other triviality case of SM7. Products give the tensor, and the function-complex formula $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(K,L)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(K\times\Delta^n,L)$ gives its adjunction and cotensor degree by degree. All simplicial sets are cofibrant and precisely the Kan complexes are fibrant. Hence its bifibrant enriched subcategory is the simplicial category of small Kan complexes. The already proved localization equivalence identifies its coherent nerve with the infinity category $\mathcal S$ of small spaces under the space convention in the statement.
